command_template: python3 tools/debian_native_container_probe.py CLIENT VERIFIED_DEB DEB_SHA256 VERIFIED_SKILL_ZIP SKILL_SHA256

container.server_network: joined only the disposable route-free DNS/TLS/HTTP fixture namespace
container.fixture_ca: copied one controlled public test CA certificate into container

repair_during_probe: The first Codex replay completed guarded calls, but a cleanup race stopped the container before package-removal proof. The probe moved removal and residue checks to the parent process; both clients passed after the fix.
timeout_cleanup_regression: Forced 1-second and 5-second harness deadlines failed as intended. The parent sent SIGTERM, allowed the harness cleanup path to finish, and verified no owned network namespace, container, or /tmp/outbound-cancel-* directory remained. Both full native client replays passed after this change.
limits: Native clients ran on the Ubuntu host; the installed MCP server ran inside the Debian 12 container.
The native harness binary_sha256 field identifies its generated launcher in this replay. The installed package executable identity is verified separately by the container probe and recorded above.
The downloaded CI artifact checksum manifest was checked; this replay did not locally verify a cryptographic attestation.
The tested package is experimental and predates any owner-approved exact release candidate; no current-version upgrade or configuration migration was tested here.
This finite TLS/DNS/recovery workflow does not prove automatic triggering, Cursor behavior, UI cancellation, all network paths or traffic through other tools.
